scope: New services/drive-sensitive-content-filter.js: redacts explicit-content signals and PII-shaped patterns (SSN, credit card, password fields) from observation text/elements, tagging each redaction with a category (never the original value) so the UI can show a labeled placeholder without ever storing or displaying the sensitive value itself.

steps.title: Create services/drive-sensitive-content-filter.js
steps.task: The file MUST begin with a JSDoc block comment containing a line exactly '@ssot docs/products/universal-overlay/PRODUCT_HOME.md' (this is mandatory and checked by a commit gate -- omitting it will cause the commit to be rejected). After that JSDoc header: create a new file exporting redactSensitiveText(text, url) and redactSensitiveElements(elements) and redactObservation(observation). redactSensitiveText detects (a) explicit-content site domains/keywords (porn/nsfw/xxx/onlyfans-style keyword and domain regex lists) -- if matched, return { text: a fixed marker string, redacted: true, category: 'explicit' }, never the original text. (b) PII-shaped patterns: SSN-shaped \d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4} and 13-16 digit credit-card-shaped sequences -- replace matched spans with a fixed marker, return { text: replaced, redacted: true, category: 'pii' } if any replacement happened. If nothing matched, return { text: original, redacted: false, category: null }. redactSensitiveElements maps over an elements array (each element has a .text and optional .type field): if el.type is 'password' (case-insensitive), replace .text with the fixed marker and tag category 'password'; otherwise run el.text through redactSensitiveText and replace if redacted. redactObservation takes an { url, title, text, elements } observation object, runs text through redactSensitiveText(text, url), runs elements through redactSensitiveElements, and returns a new observation object (do not mutate the input) with the redacted text/elements plus a top-level _redactions array listing every category that was redacted in this observation (e.g. ['password'] or ['explicit']) so callers can log that redaction occurred without knowing what was redacted. Default export an object with all three functions. Include a JSDoc header stating this is heuristic v1 (domain/keyword/pattern matching for the clearest cases only, not a full content classifier) -- do not claim complete coverage anywhere in the file. No side effects, no I/O, no imports beyond nothing (pure functions only) -- must be independently unit-testable with zero dependencies.
non_goals: a full content-classifier model call -- pure pattern matching only
